name: Institute for Biodiversity and Protected Areas
territory_ids: bijagos-archipelago; orango-national-park; joao-vieira-poilao; urok-community-mpa; cacheu-region; cacheu-mangroves-park
role: Created in 2004 to protect and manage Guinea-Bissau's biodiversity through the National System of Protected Areas, which covers about 26% of the national territory. It coordinates management of the Bijagós World Heritage property and manages the Cacheu park. Its 2006 annual report records the appointment of wardens for the Orango, João Vieira–Poilão and Cacheu parks; current park-level arrangements were not re-verified.

name: BioGuinea Foundation
role: Conservation trust fund established in 2011 as a long-term financing mechanism for Guinea-Bissau's protected areas, with funding channelled through IBAP. It supports Orango National Park, runs the Blue Bijagós project and runs a community REDD+ project in the Cacheu and Cantanhez parks. It is listed as a member of the Consortium of African Funds for the Environment (CAFÉ).
role_source_ids: gef-bioguinea-2011; bioguinea-about; bioguinea-bijagos; bioguinea-blue-bijagos; fbg-annual-report-2025; cafe-members

name: Tiniguena – Esta Terra é Nossa
role: Guinean NGO that supported the creation and participatory governance of the Urok Islands Community Marine Protected Area.

name: Wetlands International (West Africa)
role: With IBAP and partners, ran a 2015–2018 initiative to conserve and restore the Cacheu mangroves, including ecological restoration of abandoned rice fields, solar salt and a fuel-efficient fish-smoking oven. It reports that its support has improved the conservation status of 82,000 hectares of mangroves across the Cacheu and Cantanhez parks. In Liberia's Lake Piso reserve it has supported improved stoves and a cassava processing unit under an EU-funded mangrove project.

name: International Union for Conservation of Nature
role: Provided technical assistance to the coastal planning that led to the 1996 Bolama-Bijagós Biosphere Reserve. Awarded Ras Mohammed National Park IUCN Green List certification in November 2018 after an evaluation against 50 indicators.

name: The Restoration Initiative
role: Restoration programme uniting 10 countries and three Global Environment Facility agencies (IUCN, FAO and UNEP). Its Guinea-Bissau project works with women on Elia Island, near the mouth of the Cacheu River. The reviewed source does not say which agency leads the Guinea-Bissau project.

name: Regional Partnership for Coastal and Marine Conservation in West Africa
role: Regional coalition for the conservation and sustainable management of West Africa's coastal and marine areas. It partners with Rainforest Trust on a proposed project supporting new marine protected area designations in the Bijagós.

name: Rainforest Trust
role: Raising funds, with PRCM, to support government designation of four new marine protected areas in the Bijagós, including three island community MPAs (proposed project).

name: Acção para o Desenvolvimento
role: National NGO supporting a network of environmental schools (EVA) around the park.

name: CE3C – Centre for Ecology, Evolution and Environmental Changes (University of Lisbon)
role: Runs a research project on the ecological integrity of the Bijagós as a key site for waders on the East Atlantic Flyway, with partners including Tiniguena. Helped develop the biodiversity and threat monitoring protocol used in Obô Natural Park of São Tomé since 2021, and a CE3C researcher reviewed the Malanza mangrove plan.

name: Centre National de Gestion des Réserves de Faune
role: Benin's national wildlife-reserve agency; supervising administration of the Bouche du Roy marine protected area inside the reserve.

name: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit
role: Implemented the 2013–2019 project, funded by the German International Climate Initiative, that prepared the transboundary biosphere reserve.

name: IUCN National Committee of the Netherlands
role: Worked with local partners, GIZ and both governments to create the reserve, and partners Eco-Benin on blue-carbon mangrove work.

name: Eco-Benin
role: Beninese NGO running mangrove restoration and sacralisation and a blue-carbon project in the Bouche du Roy area of the reserve.

name: Hydrocarbon Pollution Remediation Project
role: Federal agency under the Ministry of Environment carrying out the Ogoniland clean-up, mangrove restoration and livelihood programmes, and preparing the Ramsar site management plan.

name: United Nations Environment Programme
role: Carried out the 2011 independent environmental assessment of Ogoniland whose recommendations frame the clean-up.

name: Fundação Maio Biodiversidade
role: Maio NGO that managed the Salinas under a 2012 delegation, monitors its birds and turtles, and leads co-management of Maio's protected areas.

name: Direção Nacional do Ambiente (Cabo Verde)
role: National environment directorate with the mandate and authority on biodiversity and conservation in Cabo Verde.

name: Office Ivoirien des Parcs et Réserves
role: Holds delegated management of the national-park part of the Ramsar site.

name: West Africa Coastal Areas Management Program (WACA)
role: World Bank-financed coastal resilience programme; funded mangrove restoration with OIPR in Côte d'Ivoire and mangrove planting in Togo.

name: Wildlife Division, Forestry Commission of Ghana
role: Management authority of the Keta Lagoon Complex Ramsar Site, mandated to enforce the law.

name: A Rocha Ghana
role: Ran the 2021–2023 PAPBio mangrove restoration and livelihoods project in four Keta Lagoon communities, with the Wildlife Division.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement (Togo)
role: Its staff act against unsustainable logging, fishing and illegal hunting at the site; it is the implementing agency of WACA in Togo.

name: Climate Technology Centre and Network
role: UNFCCC technology body that prepared a 2025 technical-assistance plan for women-led mangrove restoration and solar fish preservation in Togo's Maritime Region.

name: Parc National du Banc d'Arguin
role: Public administrative body that manages the park under its own law (2000-024).

name: BACoMaB Trust Fund (Fonds Fiduciaire du Banc d'Arguin et de la Biodiversité Côtière et Marine)
role: Conservation trust fund created in 2009 that provides long-term funding for the park, including sea surveillance and shared governance.

name: Direction des Parcs Nationaux (Senegal)
role: Named as the park's managing body in the 1993 Ramsar sheet; UNESCO names it as a partner in integrated management planning.

name: Océanium
role: Senegalese marine conservation association that proposed and led the Bamboung community marine protected area project.

name: TRY Oyster Women's Association
role: Community-based non-profit founded in 2007 that holds exclusive cockle and oyster use rights in Tanbi; it received the Equator Prize in 2012.

name: Department of Parks and Wildlife Management (The Gambia)
role: Has managed the Tanbi Wetlands Complex since 2005 and assists with enforcement under the shellfish co-management plan.

name: Coastal Resources Center, University of Rhode Island
role: Implemented the USAID Ba Nafaa project, with WWF, that supported the Tanbi shellfish co-management plan.

name: Guinée Écologie
role: Guinean NGO running mangrove restoration, solar salt, improved ovens and oyster pilots in the Konkouré delta, and a partner in the PROMAK protected-area project.

name: GRET
role: Leads the EU-funded PROMAK consortium (2025–2028) working towards legal protection of the Konkouré mangroves.

name: Office Guinéen des Parcs Nationaux et Réserves de Faune
role: Named as the future manager of the protected area proposed for the Konkouré mangroves.

name: National Protected Area Authority (Sierra Leone)
role: Statutory protected-area authority; carries out enforcement against encroachment at the estuary, though its mandate over wetlands is limited.

name: Freetown City Council
role: Runs mangrove planting in Freetown coastal communities under its #FreetownTheTreeTown campaign.

name: Sierra Leone Nature Guide Association
role: Ran bird-conservation and nature-guiding training around the Targreen wetland in 2024.

name: Forestry Development Authority (Liberia)
role: National authority for conservation forestry; lists the Lake Piso Multiple Sustainable Use Reserve among Liberia's protected areas.

name: Environmental Protection Agency of Liberia
role: Named in the 2007 Ramsar sheet as the agency responsible for the Lake Piso wetland.

name: Women United for Development
role: Grantee of a 2016–2017 GEF small-grant project on sustainable fishing at Lake Piso.

name: African Parks
role: Manages Iona under a long-term agreement signed in December 2019 with the Angolan environment ministry and the national biodiversity institute, covering law enforcement, wildlife monitoring, giraffe reintroductions and community programmes.

name: Instituto Nacional da Biodiversidade e Áreas de Conservação
role: Angola's national biodiversity and protected-area institute; government signatory of the management agreement and partner of the park's funder.

name: Legacy Landscapes Fund
role: Funds Iona as a 'legacy landscape', with African Parks as implementing partner and the national biodiversity institute as government partner; had an environmental and social due diligence carried out (2021–2022) and contracted the consultants for the 2025 milestone review.

name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
role: Partnered in setting up a community agricultural association in Monte Negro, near Iona. Leads the Sustainable Wildlife Management Programme (EU- and AFD-funded), which works with the Kyaramacan Association in Bwabwata National Park on legal and sustainable devil's claw harvesting.

name: Department of National Museum and Monuments
role: Leads oversight of the World Heritage property, coordinates the management plan from Maun, and submitted the 2024 State of Conservation report.

name: Department of Wildlife and National Parks
role: Runs anti-poaching patrols in the property and manages human–elephant conflict through its Problem Animal Control Unit (patrols, crop-damage compensation, farmer training).

name: Department of Water and Sanitation
role: Controls the invasive Salvinia in the property with a biological control weevil (Cyrtobagous salviniae).

name: Permanent Okavango River Basin Water Commission
role: Angola–Botswana–Namibia basin commission that led the Strategic Environmental Assessment of the Cubango-Okavango basin and funded climate-smart farming projects in the buffer zone.

name: Ecoexist Trust
role: Botswana NGO based in Maun that helped the State Party identify wildlife corridors in the eastern panhandle and works with farmers on reducing elephant conflict.

name: Nature Conservation Sector, Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency
role: Responsible for nature conservation and protected-area management in Egypt, including Ras Mohammed; a 2023 study of the park lists its measures, such as mooring buoys, walkways, a USD 5 daily user fee and a reef-damage fee.

name: United Nations Development Programme
role: GEF implementing agency for the 2010–2020 protected-area financing project and for the Green Sharm El Sheikh project (approved 2022), which supports improved management of Ras Mohamed. With the Global Environment Facility, funds a Gorongosa Restoration Project programme covering park law enforcement and small grants managed by Community Natural Resources Committees.

name: Global Environment Facility
role: Funded the 2010–2020 project that supported efforts to reduce tourism impacts on Ras Mohammed's reefs, coral monitoring in South Sinai and a new permit and concession system for protected areas, and funds the Green Sharm El Sheikh project.

name: Agence Nationale des Parcs Nationaux
role: Gabon's national parks agency: manages Akanda National Park, carries out awareness, surveillance and control missions there, and co-compiled the 2024 Ramsar sheet.

name: Agence Française de Développement
role: France's development agency; from 2012 to 2018 it supported ANPN's integrated management of the protected areas around Libreville, including Akanda, and co-funded the 2023 fish study.

name: Institut de Recherches Agronomiques et Forestières (IRAF), CENAREST
role: Researchers and technicians of its hydrobiology and ichthyology laboratory carried out the 2017–2018 fish survey of the park's mangroves.

name: Wildlife Conservation Society
role: Gave technical assistance to ANPN in preparing the 2014–2018 management plan and contributed to the 2023 fish study.

name: Gorongosa Restoration Project (Gorongosa Project)
role: A locally registered NGO, established with Gregory C. Carr's foundation, that co-manages Gorongosa National Park with the Government of Mozambique and runs its conservation, science and buffer-zone development programmes.

name: Administração Nacional das Áreas de Conservação
role: Mozambique's national conservation areas authority; it commissioned the 2015 external evaluation of the park's long-term co-management agreement, and the co-manager reports close coordination with it.

name: Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
role: Holds legal authority over Bwabwata National Park, wrote its 2020/21–2029/30 management plan, and administers the hunting concessions that benefit the Kyaramacan Association.

name: Kyaramacan Association
role: Residents' association inside the park that represents residents, employs community game guards and resource monitors, runs the N//goabaca campsite and receives hunting-concession revenue.

name: Integrated Rural Development and Nature Conservation
role: Helped establish the Kyaramacan Association in 2005 and, according to the management plan, is the NGO that works most with park residents.

name: BirdLife International
role: Signed a 2017 co-management memorandum for the protected areas, led EU ECOFAC 6 support to the natural parks, helped set up threat monitoring, and rehabilitated the park headquarters at Bom Sucesso.

name: Direção das Florestas e da Biodiversidade (incl. the Obô Natural Park of São Tomé directorate)
role: Government forestry and biodiversity directorate that oversees the park; its agents carry out the park's twice-yearly biodiversity and threat monitoring.

name: Oikos – Cooperação e Desenvolvimento
role: Prepared the 2020–2025 management plans for the park's Malanza and Praia das Conchas mangroves for the park department, with CEPF funding.

name: Associação Monte Pico
role: Eco-guide association whose members maintain the park's trails and join its biodiversity and threat monitoring.

name: Marine Parks and Reserves Unit
role: Manages Mafia Island Marine Park under the Board of Trustees for Marine Parks and Reserves and carries out the park's coral reef and fish monitoring.

name: WWF Tanzania Country Office
role: Funds reef and fish monitoring in the park through the Blue Action Fund-supported RUMAKI-BAF project to strengthen marine protected area management in Rufiji, Mafia and Kilwa.

name: The Ropes of Hope Tanzania
role: Runs coral restoration trials in the park and leads the CEPF-funded Kitutia Reef restoration project with Jibondo, Chole and the park authority.

name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund
role: Funds the 2025–2026 community coral restoration project on Kitutia Reef (grant 116131).

name: Sea Sense
role: Its conservation officers patrol beaches in the Rufiji–Mafia Seascape to monitor sea turtle nesting, and it runs marine conservation outreach in Mafia District villages.

name: Uganda Wildlife Authority
role: Manages Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, including law enforcement, gorilla tourism rules and revenue sharing with neighbouring communities.

name: Conservation Through Public Health
role: Runs community health and livelihood programmes around Bwindi, including the Gorilla Conservation Coffee social enterprise and emergency food support during the COVID-19 closure.

name: International Gorilla Conservation Programme
role: A coalition of Conservation International, Fauna & Flora International and WWF that works with UWA at Bwindi, supports, with UWA and CTPH, the HUGO volunteers who herd gorillas from community land back to the park, and monitors road projects affecting it.

name: Bwindi Mgahinga Conservation Trust
role: Supports community-level interventions outside the park and provides income to community projects.

name: Institute of Tropical Forest Conservation (Mbarara University of Science and Technology)
role: Leads research and monitoring in the park.
